reasons.D: Genial, confiding first person with period diction (to-day, as it were, so far as I could see), longer loose sentences and playful asides closest to the author's relish and whimsy.
reasons.A: Chatty asides (you understand, to be sure, I confess) echo the author's confiding interjections, but many short declaratives make the rhythm choppier than the passage's long cumulative sentences.
reasons.B: Longer, even sentences and mild first-person hedging fit somewhat, but the register is plain and modern, with none of the author's exuberance, parentheticals or period flavour.
reasons.C: Clipped, deadpan sentences and dry ironic repetition (another man with a beard) run against the author's effusive, sprawling, parenthesis-laden delight.
